about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Lisa Blunt Rochester

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL UNDER CHAPTER 8 OF TITLE 5, UNITED STATES CODE, OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION RELATIN
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL UNDER CHAPTER 8 OF TITLE 5, UNITED STATES CODE, OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION RELATING TO THE WITHDRAWAL OF THE RULE...
sentences: Tariffs, a war, and a golden ballroom.
Now, we have all been there where you have submitted your paperwork, you sit for an interview, you provide references, and you are just waiting for the background check.
Jumping through hoops to prove your background check was wrong while hoping to get an apartment that you applied for is still available.
It has been proven that protecting consumers from error-filled background checks can be done.
Equifax--one of the big three credit bureaus--recognized the importance and continued to handle customer complaints, despite the Trump administration's rescission of the rule.
The Federal Government should do the same, and I urge my colleagues to join us because nobody deserves to lose their job or their home because of false or outdated information.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT--Resumed
statements.title: SAFEGUARD AMERICAN VOTER ELIGIBILITY ACT--Resumed
sentences: I rise today with a deep concern that we are balancing on a knife's edge and that if the SAVE America Act becomes law, we will undercut one of the most fundamental things that make America America--the right to vote.
Let's start with the reason that we are here today--the SAVE America Act.
It would end proven and safe voter registration systems, including online and mail registration.
It would undermine voting by mail, and it would criminalize election workers, and more.
So unless they can prove their citizenship with their birth certificate or social security card, those millions of Americans will not be able to vote.
So if you can't find your birth certificate or social security card, there is now a pricetag on your access to the ballot.

Not only will they have to provide proof of citizenship, but under this bill, they also would have to bring their marriage certificate to a voting booth, or maybe a signed affidavit from a judge proving their name change.
Bottom line: If this bill passes, a driver's license, REAL ID, travel ID, college IDs for students, or military IDs will no longer be enough.

If this bill passes, you would have to mail in a photocopy of your proof of citizenship with your ballot, making it exponentially harder for Americans to vote by mail, not to mention undermining privacy.
The second comes from across the street, where the Supreme Court has been chipping and chipping and chipping away at voting rights.
The systematic weakening of our voter protections started decades ago when the Supreme Court undermined the preclearance provisions of the Voting Rights Act, the VRA.
Once it was struck down, some States began to take advantage, passing restricted voting ID laws, restricting voter registration timeframes, reducing early voting, and more.
In 2021, the Supreme Court made it harder to prove racially discriminatory voting practices under the VRA.
They pulled information from the Social Security Administration and the Internal Revenue Service.

They also raided a Georgia voting center under false pretenses, undermined access to mail-in ballots by changing the rules around how mail is postmarked, and sued and threatened States like Minnesota over access to their voter files--all of this from a President that wants to ``take over the voting'' so that the GOP ``will never lose a race for 50 years.'' This is a coordinated and un-American campaign against the very core of who we are as a nation.

Many of the rights enumerated in the 13th, 14th and 15th Amendments-- including the right to vote--were being eroded, washed away by partisan gerrymandering, poll taxes, grandfather clauses, Jim Crow laws, and even Supreme Court decisions.
If the SAVE America Act passes, we are on the verge of another contraction.
Once again, the Supreme Court is postured to send us backward, rather than protecting the path forward.
First, we must block the SAVE America Act from advancing any further.
But our democracy has contracted too, and we need to learn from that past if we are going to prevent further contraction in the future.

I look around this room, and I know that we have a choice to make: whether we will allow partisan divides to enable the backsliding of our democracy, or if we are willing to stand shoulder to shoulder to protect the bedrock of our Nation--the right to vote.
As Democratic Senators, we plan to stand in its path, and I hope that some of my Republican colleagues will join us.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONSOLIDATED APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed--Continued
statements.title: CONSOLIDATED APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed--Continued
sentences: They should be following the same rules as our State and local police officers follow in our States.
Because what we are hearing is their efforts right now are making it even more difficult for law enforcement to do their jobs and keep us safe.

I hope they will join us in making sure that not only do we continue to have public safety that includes the public and our law enforcement, but that we reform an Agency that has received over $75 billion as a slush fund.
We want to make sure that money is targeted, that people are trained, and that they are doing what is right and that they are doing at least what our State and local police officers do.
I will tell you, in listening to the speeches that came before me--such powerful words--I thought to myself, What can I actually contribute to this moment?
We will be celebrating Black History Month, and at a time where history is trying to be replaced--erased--I think it is important to think back on the things that we have been through.
And I will not be voting for this package if we do not pull out DHS and have those reforms that we spoke of.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ANNIVERSARY OF JANUARY 6
statements.title: ANNIVERSARY OF JANUARY 6
sentences: Mr. President, today is January 6, 2026.
But while there is much to look forward to on this cold winter night, I find myself transported back 5 years ago to January 6, 2021.
On January 6, I was a Member of the House of Representatives.
Five years after January 6, we are faltering once again.

From efforts to dismantle the Department of Education and the EPA to the weaponization of the Department of Justice, to active efforts to strip birthright citizenship, the Federal Government is losing its ability to protect many of the blessings of liberties we have come to expect as Americans.
Protect it like we did on January 6 and pass it on.
We will celebrate the 250th anniversary of the founding of our country.

I recalled a piece of Scripture that tells us ``all things work together for the good,'' even the bad, because despite the violence, despite the trauma, despite how close we were to losing our democracy, brave men and women stood up to protect this institution, and we will never ever, ever forget them.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: But, in reality, it would kick millions of Americans off their ACA healthcare coverage.
And to top it all off, this bill adds new abortion restrictions.
They spent 6 months before that, in the beginning of the year, passing tax cuts for billionaires.
The very first bill I sponsored--I cosponsored--as a U.S. Senator, back in January, was the Healthcare Affordability Act, which would have permanently extended the ACA tax credits.
Just last week, Senator Marshall and I introduced the PBM Disclosure Act together, a bill regarding PBM transparency.
Unfortunately, I cannot support what is being proposed here today.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Healthcare (Executive Session)
statements.title: Healthcare (Executive Session)
sentences: Like many Senators here, my office has received phone calls and emails about how devastating a lapse in ACA tax credits would be for our constituents.
He said: My family's ACA premium will increase 110 percent without the continuation of the enhanced premium subsidy.

It is time we approach the healthcare crisis with the urgency our constituents deserve, which is why tomorrow I will be introducing a new bill, the Restoring Patient Protections and Affordability Act.

Senator Wyden and I are introducing this bill because it is time for Congress to stand up for people like James and his family because no one should have to choose between rent and healthcare, between groceries and a checkup, between keeping the lights on or paying for chemo.
We have no time to waste, and I urge my colleagues to consider my bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed
statements.title: CONTINUING APPROPRIATIONS AND EXTENSIONS ACT, 2026--Motion to Proceed
sentences: I came prepared to talk about the importance of the ACA tax credits, and as I sat here, I prayed: What do I even say in this moment?

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
statements.title: TRUMP ADMINISTRATION
sentences: The Department of Defense is trying to censor the press.
It is an unprecedented move by Federal judges appointed by Democrats and Republicans alike that are speaking out on an impending judicial crisis over the Supreme Court's emergency orders.

The people need a President for all of the people--not a $20 billion bailout for Argentina, not a new White House gold ballroom when people can't even afford to pay their rent or to buy a home on their own--and not a Justice Department bailout--all while November 1 is fast approaching and tens of millions of Americans face this healthcare crisis: rising cost or a total elimination of their healthcare or medical debt.

As you talked about the small businesses, Senator, I was reminded that, as we look at who is actually purchasing this healthcare in the marketplace--a lot of people don't even know they are on ACA and receiving the tax credit--that half of them are small businesses.
Here, the voices of our communities hold weight, and that is why I stand with you as you ring the alarms.
And we are fighting for families across America who are about to see their healthcare coverage go up or maybe even be eliminated.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL UNDER CHAPTER 8 OF TITLE 5, UNITED STATES CODE, OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY RELATING TO "EM
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISAPPROVAL UNDER CHAPTER 8 OF TITLE 5, UNITED STATES CODE, OF THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY RELATING TO "EMISSIONS BUDGET AND ALLOWANCE...
sentences: How do we restore the belief that a more perfect union is even possible?
As a matter of fact, in Delaware, a union leader said to me: You can't spell ``labor'' without ``L-B-R.'' I know jobs.
And I can tell you, we need a new and different approach to jobs in this country, especially as we look to the future of work in the age of artificial intelligence.
The groundbreaking research from that era still impacts us today--GPS systems, weather satellites, the COVID-19 vaccine, even the internet.
Our Nation's zoning frameworks date back to the 1920s--100 years ago.
Together, we can expand housing supply, build stronger communities, make housing more attainable, unlock innovative housing models, and invest in smart tax policy.
Not every family looks the same, but we all want the same things: quality healthcare, affordable childcare, and the comfort of knowing that Social Security and Medicare will be there for us too.
We have an opportunity to provide peace of mind and create jobs by investing in childcare and healthcare, but that is only half the battle.
Who doesn't want clean drinking water and clean air?
But for many across this country, there are Ellendales everywhere, many communities that still need champions in this Chamber, especially as we confront the threats of climate change.
As the junior Senator from the lowest lying State in the Nation, from our farms and our beaches to our environmental justice communities, in Delaware, we know climate change is real.
I have bright hope because I prayed in the Gallery on January 6, and I am here, alive, standing firm for democracy and love.
It was clear that if we can help Americans live their purpose, provide peace, and protect our planet, I believe we will be able to rebuild the trust we have lost.
But I will never forget the exhilaration I felt on the day we moved into our own home, a place that was truly ours.
And I will never forget the look of frustration in her eyes.
Mr. President, I will end where I began--with bright hope.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Rescission (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: Rescission (Executive Calendar)
sentences: Mr. President, I thank the Presiding Officer and I thank, also, Senator Durbin for providing this opportunity to speak up against this rescissions package.
So to bring it back to where I started with Mr. Rogers, I urge my colleagues to stop what they have planned because it is wrong.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: Today, Medicaid is the single largest payer of maternity care in the United States, covering 40 percent of births nationwide and nearly half of all births in our rural communities.
To be blunt, now is not the time to be slashing the Medicaid program.
My amendment would stop cuts to Medicaid used for vital hospital services, especially for labor and delivery rooms.
Leader Thune said it himself earlier today, that Medicaid should be for pregnant moms.
Do we stand for billionaires or do we stand up for moms and babies?
For Democrats, the choice is clear, and I urge my Republican colleagues to vote yes on the motion to support families over billionaires.

statements.title: H.R. 1
sentences: Mr. President, I ask unanimous consent that the text of the motions to commit be printed in the Record: Motion to Commit With Instructions Ms. Blunt Rochester moves to commit the bill H.R. 1 to the Committee on Finance of the Senate with instructions to report the same back to the Senate in 3 days, not counting any day on which the Senate is not in session, with changes that-- (1) are within the jurisdiction of such committee; (2) would strike any provision limiting Medicaid state- directed payments; and (3) would preserve access to hospital labor and delivery units to protect the 40% of births nationwide and nearly 50% of births in rural communities that are financed by Medicaid.

Motion to Commit With Instructions Ms. BLUNT ROCHESTER moves to commit the bill H.R. 1 to the Committee on Finance of the Senate with instructions to report the same back to the Senate in 3 days, not counting any day on which the Senate is not in session, with changes that- (1) are within the jurisdiction of such committee; and (2) would create an above-the-line tax deduction for primary care, dental, and mental health workers serving in Health Professional Shortage Areas.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Abortion (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: Abortion (Executive Calendar)
sentences: Three years ago, I marched with my House colleagues to the Supreme Court.
On that day, Roe v. Wade was overturned, and for many, their lives were turned upside down.
Since then, extreme Republicans and President Trump have said that abortion is a States' rights issue--States' rights.

Yet, over the last 3 years, we have watched as quietly and purposefully they have chipped away at our rights, chipped away at our bodily autonomy, because the goal has always been a national abortion ban.
Three Trump-appointed Supreme Court Justices and the Dobbs decision later and we are still watching this unfold.
Anti-abortion extremists have been piecing together a puzzle that, when it is completed, will create a national abortion ban, and they add a new piece each and every day.

Over the next hour, my colleagues and I will lay out what the Republican national abortion ban looks like, what it means for everyday Americans, and what we can do about it because these efforts will hurt all of us--especially young women, women of low income, women in rural areas, and women of color.

We are here today to show the American people that we did not forget about the Dobbs decision, especially because the majority of Americans--Democrats, Republicans, and Independents--believe that we should have legal and safe abortions.

You can't claim to be the party of strong economic growth while cutting Medicaid, food assistance, and childcare for many women who need it to participate in the workforce--and all to give tax breaks to people who already have all of these resources.
And when it is completed, it will strip Americans of their access to abortion care in red States and blue States.

Whether you call it a ``Big Bad Bill'' or whether you call it a ``Big Ugly Bill,'' whatever you call it, this is the moment for people to speak up because it is just another piece of the puzzle, and we are here to shine a light on the ultimate goal of a national abortion ban.

This very week, we potentially will see a bill on this floor that will again chip away--chip away--at healthcare, when we know that 40 percent of the births in this country are through Medicaid; chip away at our rights.

Just a few weeks before I received my diagnosis, the Supreme Court issued the decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization, overturning Roe v. Wade and eliminating the legal right to abortion.
The fallout from that decision was fast, with states across the country starting to enforce cruel and dangerous abortion bans.

My home state of Louisiana has some of the strictest abortion laws in the country, and even though I needed to terminate my pregnancy to protect my own health and safety, I was told I could not receive care at the hospital in Baton Rouge.
Instead of being able to process the diagnosis and grieve the loss of the pregnancy at home with my family, I had to scramble to find a way out of Louisiana to access abortion care.
I will end with a story of an individual who I just met today.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ALEX PADILLA
statements.title: ALEX PADILLA
sentences: I will continue to stand with Alex Padilla.
I will continue to stand with those folks around this country who are facing this same kind of unacceptable behavior.

statements.title: MEDICAID
sentences: And late, late last night, House Republicans added even more distress to their Medicaid cuts, changes that would cut care and prevent access to care for millions of Americans; changes that would cut funding that ensures safe, healthy births for newborns; changes that will endanger our parents and grandparents who live in nursing homes.

So I rise today and seek true compassion from my colleagues and ask in the words of the famous song: ``Where is the love?'' I rise today because I have been getting call after call, email after email, meeting with person after person, all worried sick about cuts to Medicaid.
I want my colleagues to hear their names and understand the trade-offs they are making to support tax cuts for the wealthy, while failing to shrink the national debt.
Again, I am going to say that again: while failing to shrink the national debt.
When I met with him recently, he told me that if we pull the thread of Medicaid, his whole life would unravel.
For Emmanual, Medicaid is more than prescriptions and doctors' appointments.
Participating in Medicaid allowed him to get and keep a job.
Access to Medicaid is how he went from being homeless to being employed, housed, and financially secure.
And you guessed it; Point of Hope is funded through Medicaid.
She doesn't know where her son will end up if they lose the support that Medicaid provides and she can no longer take care of him.
As a result, he is on a Medicaid waiver since he was 8 months old.
Medicaid covers the medical equipment Nancy rents to keep Christopher alive.
Medicaid covers the skilled medical professionals that help Nancy care for her son and give her respite.
These are real people with real needs that Medicaid fills--real people whom we shine the light on and not ignore.

So whether you are a person of faith or just somebody who cares about your neighbor, now is the time to move from the Golden Rule of treating others as you would like to be treated to the ``Platinum Rule''--to treat others the way they want to be treated, with real compassion, and to start with protecting Medicaid.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: It is a simple, straightforward piece of legislation that will protect American consumers by prohibiting tariffs that increase the costs of building a house.
Our closest ally to the north is now on the receiving end of a senseless trade war.
Essential groceries and food products, building supplies, materials that impact our national security, all of these things and more that cross the border are now each and every day in jeopardy.
I recently asked the Federal Reserve Chairman: Are tariffs a tax?
And he said: Well, you will pay either the tariff at the exporter level, the importer, the retailer, and/or the consumer.
You have nearly $40,000 in investment that you were ready to sell to cover your downpayment.
That $400,000 home that you were eyeing has been on the market for a few months now, but then this administration slaps tariffs on half the world, and the market drops.
There goes your downpayment and your dream of homeownership.
But with the tariffs, what would have once been covered by what you saved--now it is just a drop in the bucket.
A house is made of many imported materials, and these tariffs increase the amount consumers will have to spend each and every step along the way.
Let's look at a new build from the ground up and how the President's tariffs will make it more expensive.
Cement is a key component in laying the foundation of a home, and these tariffs could raise the price of cement alone 18 percent--just the foundation increased by 18 percent.
For so many across our Nation, these tariffs mean more than an increase in price.

Now, I am pretty sure that President Trump ran on an agenda of lowering costs, but what we are seeing here are broken promises and a shakedown of working families to line the pockets of his billionaire friends.
I am sorely disappointed that my Republican colleagues refuse to stand up for their States and their constituents despite knowing how harmful these tariffs will be.
Madam President, yesterday when the budget resolution came to the floor, I introduced an amendment.
I urge my colleagues to vote no on this budget resolution.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
statements.title: LEGISLATIVE SESSION
sentences: It means higher prescription drug costs for seniors, which we fought so hard to lower.
While Republicans work to cut taxes for billionaires, they are slashing the healthcare workforce our communities rely on.
On behalf of our constituents and our country, I urge my colleagues to support this amendment.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NOMINATION OF ROBERT F. KENNEDY, JR.
statements.title: NOMINATION OF ROBERT F. KENNEDY, JR.
sentences: I have thought about senior citizens in my State who are on Medicare and children with special needs who may be on Medicaid, and the fact that in our hearing and also in my one-on-one conversation with him, he confused the two.

I think about her ability to have reproductive freedom over her own life, when Mr. Kennedy has changed his positions so many times on where he stands on reproductive freedom and the right for her to choose what she wants for her life.
It is important to me that the person who holds this job understands those basic things--Medicare, Medicaid, EMTALA-- and that we face a challenge for women's lives being saved.

Mr. President, on the eve of the vote for the nominee for the Department of Health and Human Services, I stand before you acknowledging that I will vote no on the confirmation of Mr. Robert F. Kennedy.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Trump Executive Orders (Executive Calendar)
statements.title: Trump Executive Orders (Executive Calendar)
sentences: Police and fire departments up and down the State of Delaware could go unfunded.
Children of working families could go hungry when free lunch programs stop.
But with the stroke of a pen, President Trump tried to defund programs already signed into law, making Delaware and every other State across the country less safe, less healthy, and less stable.
Here is what the White House Press Secretary, Karoline Leavitt, posted on X: This is NOT a rescission of the federal funding freeze.
It is simply a rescission of the OMB memo.

Beyond this unlawful budget freeze, this administration and an unelected and unchecked billionaire have threatened and, in some cases, delivered on massive civil servant layoffs and unconstitutional firings.
Some say to give tax breaks not to all, but to billionaires--or, as I call it, reverse Robin Hood.
From USAID to the Department of Labor to Treasury to the thought of abolishing the Department of Education, everyone will be impacted.
Public safety: Grants for law enforcement and homeland security activities will cease.
Public transit could be halted, including projects already under construction.
Head Start and childcare could be affected: Funding for Head Start Programs that provide comprehensive early childhood education for more than 800,000 kids and their families could be cut off.

Our veterans, who have served us so mightily: Federal grants to help veterans in rural areas access healthcare and grants to help veterans get other critical services, including suicide prevention resources, transition assistance, and housing for homeless veterans could be cut off.
They are preschool and infrastructure.

Should these organizations close their doors, seniors would go hungry, people facing mental health crises would not have critical assistance, at- risk children would be more vulnerable to abuse, justice- involved individuals would be far more likely to re-offend, and sexual assault survivors would be forced to deal with their trauma alone.

They said to me: The loss of federal funds would significantly impact our ability to continue offering vital programs such as Harm Reduction, Pregnant & Parenting Women, and Building Communities of Recovery, as well as halt the building and renovation of two new recovery homes.

The prospective partnerships which are currently in development with the Department of Public Health and Department of Education in the area of infant early childhood mental health consultation would likely not move forward.
The Coalition For a Safer Delaware: Delaware relies on it for suicide prevention, domestic violence intervention, community violence programs.
It snapped me out of my own pain, and it made me realize how blessed I am--I am going to be OK--but a lot of other people were hurting, a lot of other people were struggling.

I am going to say that one again: A prolonged freeze on these resources will only exacerbate economic instability, stifle job growth, and erode our people's trust in their government.'' I urge this Senate to act swiftly and decisively to mitigate the potentially devastating impact of this funding freeze.

And I will read some excerpts from his statement: On the federal grant pause, the short-term risk is upwards of $10 million [for DSU], which would significantly impact our ability to operate through the end of [this] fiscal year.
The Delaware Community Reinvestment Action Council: We will not be able to sustain tax representation impacting hundreds of low-income families awaiting a refund.
